description: Migration of an Airflow ETL pipeline while a data-quality incident is open: DAG backfills, schema drift, late-arriving partitions and a broken sensor.

facts.statement: The quarantined records for the migrated Airflow ETL batch were written to s3://airflow-migration-quarantine/2024-06-03/.
During the Airflow-to-Prefect cutover, the incident guardrail called `validate_partition_counts()` before promoting the new ETL DAG.
During the Airflow-to-Dagster cutover for the active null-`event_id` data-quality incident, the migration gate sets `null_event_id_abort_limit` to 2048 rows.
During the data-quality incident, the Airflow migration inventory recorded that the ETL staging tables were copied into the schema `dq_incident_20240514`.
During the active data-quality incident, the Airflow ETL migration to the new orchestration platform was gated by the `DQ_MIGRATION_AIRFLOW_HOME` environment variable name.
During the active data-quality incident, the rollback commit for the Airflow ETL migration to the new orchestration platform had the hash prefix 7b4e9a2.
During the incident, the Dagster replay of the corrupted sales_daily Airflow DAG took 133 minutes.
To keep the Airflow-to-Dagster migration moving during the freshness-monitor incident, the `migrate-etl` script required the `--allow-stale-quality-checks` flag.

The successful re-run of the migrated customer_orders ETL pipeline was the Dagster attempt `customer_orders/attempt-04`, following the active data-quality incident that invalidated `customer_orders/attempt-03`.
During the active data-quality incident, the Airflow-to-Dagster migration pinned pyarrow==12.0.1 in the requirements lockfile.
While migrating the Airflow ETL pipeline during the data-quality incident, the migration inventory listed the legacy Sales ETL DAG at /opt/airflow/dags/legacy_sales_etl.py.
During the Airflow migration incident, the UI proxy health check was pinned to TCP port 9721 instead of the default 8080.

messages.text: Complete the pipeline migration while keeping the nightly data-quality checks green.

New symptom: after Airflow 2.10.5 dagrun_timeout change, Prefect migration runner raises KeyError: 'data_quality_incident_id' in flows/etl_migration.py inside run_backfill(). ETL_ORCH_ENV=staging. Repro: poetry run pytest tests/test_incident_guard.py -k timeout; frame validate_incident_context line 143. Airflow logs retry storm on tasks/load_gold.py.

I’m summarizing migration status for the `daily_orders_etl` Airflow DAG in `/opt/airflow/dags/etl/orders.py` (Airflow 2.9.3, `catchup=False`, `max_active_runs=1`). I mapped tasks `extract_orders` (line 41), `validate_customer_key` (line 58), `load_golden_orders` (line 77) to candidate tasks in `/orchestrator/prefect/flows/orders_flow.py` using Prefect 3.0.4 and `flow.from_source`. During the active data-quality incident, I preserved the `dq_check_orders_v3` SQL query from `/dbt/models/staging/orders_quality.sql` and thresholds `null_order_id>0.001` and `duplicate_key>0.002`, but I have not confirmed whether the new platform’s retry flag `retries=2, retry_delay_seconds=300` reproduces Airflow’s `execution_timeout=1800` and `sla=1200` semantics. Remaining unknown: whether the failing partition is caused by `extract_orders` timezone handling (`local_tz=UTC` vs scheduler `America/Los_Angeles`) or the dbt incremental `--vars '{"target_partition": ...}'` not passing into Prefect context, so no final fix yet.

Please verify your earlier claim that migration/airflow_to_dagster.py maps Airflow 2.7.3 retries to Prefect 2.14 backfills during the dq_incident. Run pytest tests/test_backfill.py -k dq_incident and confirm DQ_SEVERITY=2 propagates through execute_etl() in jobs/warehouse_load.py without hitting the old airflow.operators.postgres_operator stack frame.

The last tool output implies that the Airflow DAG `sales_reconciliation_v2` is still executing the legacy `PostgresOperator` task `load_fact_sales` even after the Temporal workflow stub was registered. In `dags/sales_reconciliation.py:84`, the `default_args` remain pinned to `retries=2` and `retry_delay=timedelta(minutes=5)`, so a data-quality timeout will not fail fast; it will create three duplicate load attempts. The `airflow dags test sales_reconciliation_v2 2026-02-14 --no-parse` output also shows `airflow.providers.postgres.operators.postgres.PostgresOperator` deprecation against Airflow 2.9.3, and the Temporal worker log confirms the `load_fact_sales` activity is never reached because the pre-flight `validate_source_counts` hook returns exit code 1. This suggests the new orchestrator adapter is wired correctly, but the old Airflow path is still being used by the active incident runbook and may be amplifying inconsistent row counts.

Scope change: pause Prefect 2.14 migration of etl_daily.py. During incident, only add data-quality gate in airflow/dags/quality_checks.py before load_to_snowflake(): fail if row_count<100000 or null_pct>0.05 in order_events. Keep Airflow 2.9.3; set DAG_ID=daily_etl and run airflow dags test daily_etl 2024-05-01, then resume migration postmortem.

The last `kubectl logs -p airflow-webserver-...` output implies the cutover gate is not met: at `migrator/config/target_platform.yaml:41` the `scheduler_name` is `prefect-agent` under Prefect 2.16.1 while the running pod annotation `orchestration.target=smaug` says `smaug-agent`, so the reconciler fell back to the legacy Airflow 2.10.2 executor at `migrator/executor/adapter.go:187` and skipped the dual-write shim. The incident signal is not just schema drift; the `dag_id=customer_revenue_daily_v3` run failed validation because the expected `manifest_checksum=7d3c...` from `etl/quality/snapshots/2026-02-18.json` is absent from the target artifact. That means the new platform cannot attest which transformation version emitted the bad partitions, so any rollback or backfill would be unsafe until the mapping table in `migrator/dag_id_alias.py:22` is corrected and the `--emit-compatibility-manifest` flag is reenabled.

Hypothesis: the dq_incident is not caused by the new platform runtime itself but by a stale scheduler dependency in the migration bundle. In /migrate/airflow_to_tempo/dags/sales_fact_daily.py line 214, the Airflow task `transform_sales` still emits `sales_fact_temp` via the legacy `BashOperator`, while the new `sales_fact_final` materialization depends on `load_sales` at line 228. The platform manifest at /migrate/tempo/jobs/sales_fact_daily.yaml, version 2.7.1, maps `load_sales` to `job-sales-fact-final`, but does not include `sales_fact_temp` as an upstream output. If `/var/log/tempo/job-sales-fact-final.2026-03-05.log` shows `dq.check.row_count_delta=+18.4%` immediately after the first parallel run, and `airflow dags show sales_fact_daily --output dot` still lists the BashOperator edge, that confirms the old temporary table is feeding a partially migrated lineage. I would next inspect `SELECT * FROM sales_fact_temp WHERE etl_batch_id = '2026-03-05T00:00:00Z'` against `sales_fact_final`.

Do not apply the fallback in etl_transform.py normalize_nulls() yet. We are mid-incident in dq_pipeline, and changing transform logic while Airflow 2.7.2 tasks feed Prefect 3.1.0 can hide the real cause. Set DQ_ALLOW_MISSING_PARTITION=false, re-run python scripts/replay_dag.py --dag-id daily_sales --task-id extract_orders --date 2024-06-14, and capture the stack frame from extract_orders first.

I’ll inspect `dags/etl/revenue_quality_dag.py` next, specifically lines 60-140, because the incident alert names `dq_check_revenue_null_rate` and `dq_check_currency_variance`. The Airflow 2.8.1 DAG declares those checks with `trigger_rule='all_done'` and `pool='dq_critical'`, but the migration stub in `migrations/prefect_2.19/revenue_flow.py` currently maps only line 78 `dq_check_revenue_null_rate` to a Prefect task with `retries=2`, while line 112 `dq_check_currency_variance` still uses a TODO timeout and no `on_failure` hook. That gap could explain why bad rows were not blocked during the 02:10 UTC run while the scheduler reported task success. I also want to compare `config/orchestration_overrides.yaml` line 37, `fail_on_quality_threshold: false`, against the old Airflow `airflow.cfg` scheduler default `catchup=True`. If the new platform ignores that flag or the DAG’s `sla=30m`, the incident may be a migration semantics issue rather than source-data corruption. I won’t patch yet; first confirm whether the missing failure hook is the trigger.

During the Airflow-to-Prefect cutover, the incident guardrail called `validate_partition_counts()` before promoting the new ETL DAG.

We can keep Airflow 2.7.3 as source of truth for now. The data-quality incident is in etl/ingest_orders.py validate_amounts() due to NULL amount_cents after OrdersDelta DQ check. For the platform migration, create a shadow DAG in airflow/dags/migration/ named orders_dq_shadow that reads the same Spark output and writes comparison metrics to dq.metrics before cutting over. Do not modify prod DAGs yet.

Before continuing the migration, I checked the data-quality incident against the current Airflow DAG and the candidate Temporal workflow. The prior suspicion was that the new platform was dropping the end_time predicate at transform_sales.py:148, causing late records to enter dwd.sales_daily. That is ruled out. Running the same partition through python -m pytest tests/test_transform_sales.py::test_end_time_filter -k late -v on Airflow 2.8.4 and on the Temporal worker image orch-migrate:2026.02.17 produced identical filtered row counts: 4,127,208 input rows, 312 filtered, 4,126,896 output. The generated SQL in artifacts/plan_20260217_14.sql contains AND s.updated_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-02-17 00:00:00+00' at line 62, and the --strict-cutoff flag is present in both dags/sales_etl.py:93 and workflows/sales_etl.yaml:77. Therefore the bad rows are not caused by the predicate missing under the new orchestrator; next I will compare upstream extraction timestamps and retry semantics rather than the filter.

Python 3.10.12, Airflow 2.6.3, dbt-core 1.5.2, Snowflake connector 3.1.0. DAGs in /opt/airflow/dags/finance_etl; entry load_revenue_daily. My current hypothesis is that the data-quality alerts on bronze.sales_orders are not from the migration rewrite itself but from a schedule/timezone mismatch introduced when translating Airflow 2.7.3 semantics to the new orchestrator. In dags/sales_orders_daily.py lines 118-142 the task query_sales_orders uses start_date=datetime(2024,1,1, tzinfo=timezone.utc), catchup=False, and passes execution_date={{ ds }} to BigQuery. The replacement definition in config/orchestrator/sales_orders_daily.yaml line 57 maps {{ ds }} to {{ logical_start_time }} without converting to the warehouse partition date, so 2024-06-14T23:00 UTC likely writes dt=2024-06-15 instead of dt=2024-06-14. This would explain the missing late-evening rows and the duplicate counts in the 00:00 partition. To confirm, I want the new orchestrator’s run ID and rendered SQL for run_id=so-2024-06-14-23, the BigQuery partition metadata for bronze.sales_orders dt=2024-06-14 and dt=2024-06-15, and the scheduler logs around 00:05 UTC. If rendered logical_start_time is 23:00 UTC but partition value is 2024-06-15, that confirms the mapping bug; if SQL partitions match but upstream ingest is delayed, I should rule out ingestion instead.

During the Airflow-to-Dagster cutover for the active null-`event_id` data-quality incident, the migration gate sets `null_event_id_abort_limit` to 2048 rows.

Run python -m pytest tests/test_order_idempotency.py -k duplicate with ORCH_PLATFORM=dagster and AIRFLOW_HOME=/opt/airflow, then paste the stack trace if load_orders_asset raises psycopg2.IntegrityError.

My hypothesis is that the incident is not caused by the new orchestration runtime itself, but by a partitioning mismatch between the Airflow DAG and the migrated pipeline, with Airflow 2.9.3 and Dagster 1.8.12. In /opt/airflow/dags/etl_sales_daily.py, the BashOperator at lines 118-143 runs `sales_extract.py --partition {{ ds }}` using Airflow templated `ds`, while the replacement Dagster job in /src/pipelines/sales.py:67 calls `sales_extract.py --partition ${execution_date:%Y-%m-%d}`. If Dagster's `execution_date` is being passed as a timezone-aware string instead of Airflow's UTC date, the extract may read the prior day's HDFS partition `/warehouse/sales/ds=${partition}`. That would explain late-arriving rows and NULL revenue keys in the quality incident, while the transform logic in `transform_sales.py` remains unchanged. To confirm, I need the failed Dagster run logs for run_id `sales_daily_20260214_033000`, the rendered CLI command under `DAGSTER_REPOSITORY_PATH`, and the Airflow TaskInstance log for `sales_extract` with `--verbose`. I also want to inspect the `sales_quality_checks` metric `daily_partition_key_null_count` for whether the spike starts exactly when the migration flag `USE_DAGSTER=true` was enabled in `/deploy/env/prod.yaml:42`.

I just hit this while migrating airflow_dag_to_dagster.py during dq_incident: ImportError: cannot import name 'DagsterAssetKey' from 'dagster' (version 1.9.14). During the data-quality incident, the Airflow migration inventory recorded that the ETL staging tables were copied into the schema `dq_incident_20240514`.

I have mapped the Airflow DAG definitions under /opt/airflow/dags/etl_pipeline.py, specifically the inventory_load DAG tasks on lines 87, 132, and 209, to the target platform's flow manifest at flows/inventory-migration.yaml. Airflow 2.7.3 xcoms are captured as platform context variables, and the retry logic on line 148 is represented by retry_count: 3 and backoff: 2m. During the active data-quality incident, I paused the production schedule in Airflow using airflow dags pause inventory_load and disabled the new platform's trigger with --disable-trigger while comparing warehouse counts. The remaining unknown is whether the source snapshot used by the incident investigation contains the late-arriving records from the 03:00 UTC batch, because the object storage listing for s3://warehouse/landing/inventory/2024-06-18/ is inconsistent with the Airflow log timestamp at 03:11:42 UTC. I need a checksum comparison for the 03:00 files before enabling any migrated task.

Got this while migrating the ETL to Prefect 3.0.5: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'airflow.providers.amazon.aws.sensors.s3' in dags/retail/ingest_orders.py, stack frame wait_for_s3 at sensors/order_file.py:42. Env: AIRFLOW_HOME=/opt/airflow, AIRFLOW_VERSION=2.10.4. Data-quality alert is firing on bronze.orders. Please replace the S3 sensor with boto3 and rerun the validation.

I’ve completed an initial inventory of the Airflow 2.9.3 pipeline at /opt/airflow/dags/etl_orders.py and exported the task graph from the metadata DB. DAG runs are tagged incident_id=dq-20260214-07, with failures concentrated in validate_order_quality around line 188 and transform_orders at line 247. I captured the existing SLAs: schedule=0 2 * * *, retries=3, retry_delay=5m, pool=dq_priority, and sensors waiting on s3://raw/orders/dt={{ds}}/SUCCESS. On the target Dagster 1.7.7 branch, I stubbed jobs/orders_etl.py and assets/orders_transform.py, mapping extract_orders to the upstream asset, validate_quality to a metadata-only asset, and load_warehouse to a Snowflake 3.9.0 merge. The remaining unknown is whether the current incident is caused by late-arriving SUCCESS markers, duplicate keys in the raw Parquet files, or schema drift between Airflow’s JSONPath check and the new asset-key contract. I need the raw file checksums from S3 and the exact customer_id null/dup counts before choosing how to implement an idempotent load without masking the incident.

Until the schema mapping and XCom contract are reconciled, the new platform’s failures are an artifact, not a root cause.

During the active data-quality incident, the Airflow ETL migration to the new orchestration platform was gated by the `DQ_MIGRATION_AIRFLOW_HOME` environment variable name.

Hypothesis: for INC-4521, the active data-quality break is not caused by the target orchestrator’s scheduler itself, but by a timezone/trigger compatibility difference between Airflow 2.6.2 DAGs and Temporal Python SDK 1.7.3. In `dags/etl_daily_sales.py` the old DAG used `start_date = pendulum.datetime(2024, 1, 1, tz='America/New_York')` and `schedule_interval='@daily'`, while the migrated workflow in `temporal/workflows/etl_daily_sales.py:184` is firing at 04:00 UTC because the Temporal schedule uses `cron_schedule='0 4 * * *'` without the `tz` argument. This would make late-arriving partitions from `bronze.sales_orders` miss the `event_time` filter in `sql/silver_sales_transform.sql:72`, producing duplicate `order_id` keys when the `upsert` merge retries after the first empty run. I would confirm it by querying the platform audit table for `schedule_id='sales_daily_v2'` to compare actual `scheduled_at` values against Airflow’s `execution_date` from `airflow db snapshot` for the last 3 days, and by replaying one failed run with `--dry-run --tz America/New_York` in `temporal run workflow`; if the duplicate-key count changes only when the trigger fires in New York time, the hypothesis is confirmed.

To keep the Airflow-to-Dagster migration moving during the freshness-monitor incident, the `migrate-etl` script required the `--allow-stale-quality-checks` flag.

New symptom: after moving order_quality_dag to Dagster 1.10, run_check fails in customer_orders_asset with psycopg2.ProgrammingError: 'operator does not exist: character varying = character varying[]'. Trace points to sql_checks.py line 88, but Airflow PostgresHook.get_conn() still used despite ORCHESTRATOR_BACKEND=dagster in docker-compose.yml. Did connection context or array binding change?

Looking at the incident artifacts, I’m ruling out the Airflow worker pool saturation theory. In `dags/etl/reconcile_orders.py` lines 412-417, the suspected duplicate writes would only happen if `max_active_runs` were >1, but the migrated DAG spec in `platform/target/orchestrator/job_manifest.yaml` pins `concurrency=1` and `allow_backfill=false`. The Airflow scheduler logs from `var/log/airflow/scheduler.log` show the three failed runs at 2024-06-12T02:10, 02:35, and 03:01 UTC all serialized: no parallel task instances, and the worker pool queue remained empty at 12/128. The same window in the incident data sample `warehouse/quality/anomaly_orders.csv` lacks duplicate `order_txn_id` values, only null `source_updated_at`. So the earlier hypothesis that overlapping backfills caused the row fan-out is not supported. We should keep investigating the source-side timestamp extraction rather than concurrency.

For this incident, assume Airflow 2.5.3 with PostgreSQL metadata, not the 2.10.2 image. The failure is in airflow_dags/ecommerce_etl.py at clean_orders when null_rate > 0.03. Use dbt run --select orders_cleaned and set DATA_QUALITY_STRICT=1. Do not modify legacy_s3.py yet.

I suspect the data-quality incident is not caused by the new orchestration platform itself but by the backfill trigger still pointing at the old Airflow scheduler while the migration toggle in airflow/dags/etl_user_events.py lines 58-74 has already changed schedule_interval to @daily and max_active_runs=1. On Airflow 2.10.4 the manual trigger_dag call from infra/migration/run_backfill.sh line 33 uses the deprecated --dag-id path, so it may enqueue the legacy task group rather than the migrated Dagster sensor in dags/migrated/user_events_pipeline.py line 91. If duplicates are concentrated in the events_enriched table between 02:00 and 04:00 UTC and the audit table has two execution_date partitions for the same run_id, that would confirm the old scheduler is still feeding the incident window while the new platform is only downstream validation. I will check the Airflow task instance state, the Dagster asset materialization logs, and the dbt_models/enriched_events.sql freshness metadata before changing any DAG ownership.

Confirmation would come from correlating failed rows in `quality_checks/score_completeness.sql` with partition metadata in `dagster_run_id=a7f3b2` and checking whether `airflow.cfg` `[core] timezone = utc` differs from `dagster.yaml` `timezone: America/New_York`. This would be confirmed by comparing manifest.json run timestamps in dbt/target with _SUCCESS markers, checking Athena query logs for partitions with row_count=0 around incident hours, and inspecting the platform job UI for retries disabled flag.
